title: Simultaneous parameters for transverse prime ideals and coordinate-product algebra
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative regular local ring of dimension $d$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. (a) Let $r\geq0$ and let $P_1,\ldots,P_r$ be pairwise distinct prime ideals of $R$ such that each $R/P_i$ is regular local of dimension $d-1$, and $R/(P_1+\cdots+P_r)$ is regular local with $\dim R=\dim R/(P_1+\cdots+P_r)+r$. There exists a regular system of parameters $f_1,\ldots,f_d$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters] with $r\leq d$ and $P_i=(f_i)$ for $1\leq i\leq r$. The sum over an empty family is $(0)$. (b) For any regular system of parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ and $0\leq r\leq d$, put $T=t_1\cdots t_r$, with empty product $1$. The element $T$ is a nonzerodivisor, the ideals $(t_i)$ for $i\leq r$ are pairwise incomparable primes, and $(T)=\bigcap_{i=1}^r(t_i)$ is radical. The prime ideals minimal over $(T)$ are exactly these $(t_i)$. For every subset $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ the quotient $R/(t_j:j\in J)$ is regular local of dimension $d-|J|$. For $r=0$, $(T)=R$ has no prime ideals above it; the empty ideal intersection is $R$.

source.place:
Tag 0BIA (lemma-strict-normal-crossings), both local-ring arguments; Algebra Tags 00NR (lemma-regular-quotient-regular) and 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM). Proof handoff retained verbatim under the released re-split order; these are the old parent arguments to implement, not proof steps of this statement-only node. Original parent step 2: Suppose first that $H$ is a boundary and choose its finite family $C_i$ from the boundary definition. Fix $x\in H$ and enumerate the members containing $x$ as $C_1,\ldots,C_r$, where $r\ge1$. Put $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $d=\dim R$, and let $P_i$ be the ideal of $C_i$ in $R$. The singleton conditions give that $R/P_i$ is regular local of dimension $d-1$. Apply the regular-quotient kernel theorem to $P_i$: it is generated by an initial subfamily of some regular system of parameters of $R$. The parameter-quotient dimension formula shows that this subfamily has length exactly one. Consequently choose $f_i$ with $P_i=(f_i)$. All these applications use proper ideals, since $x\in C_i$, and regular source ring $R$, since $X$ is regular.
Cited statements: def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary, lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-quotient-kernel-parameters, lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence.

Original parent step 3: The intersection condition for these $r$ members says that $Q=R/(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ is regular local and $\dim Q=d-r$; in particular $r\le d$. Choose $d-r$ generators of the maximal ideal of $Q$, and lift them to $f_{r+1},\ldots,f_d\in\mathfrak m_R$. For every $a\in\mathfrak m_R$, write its image in $Q$ as a linear combination of the chosen generators and lift the coefficients. The difference belongs to $(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$. Hence $\mathfrak m_R=(f_1,\ldots,f_d)$, and this length-$d$ list is a regular system of parameters by definition. This is the actual simultaneous parameter choice; the separate parameter systems in the preceding step are not assumed compatible.
Cited statements: def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary, def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters.

Original parent step 4: Since $H$ is reduced and its support is the union of the $C_i$, step 1 gives $\mathcal I_{H,x}=\bigcap_{i=1}^r(f_i)$. The parameter-factorization lemma says each $f_i$ is prime in the domain $R$. Distinct $f_i$ are nonassociate: after permuting the full parameter system, the image of $f_j$ in $R/(f_i)$ is a nonzerodivisor in a nonzero local ring, so is not zero. In a domain with these distinct prime factors, an element divisible by every $f_i$ is divisible by their product: induct on $r$, using primality to cancel the previously removed factors. The reverse containment is immediate. Therefore $\mathcal I_{H,x}=(f_1\cdots f_r)$. If $x\notin H$, its ideal stalk is $R$, giving the required empty product; choose any parameter system of the regular local ring $R$. This proves the forward direction, including an empty boundary.
Cited statements: lem-trf-regular-local-ufd-boundary-factorization, lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence, lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-ideal-stalk-range, def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters.

Original parent step 5: Conversely assume the stated local equation condition. At each $x$ write $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $T=t_1\cdots t_r$. The same prime-factor argument as in step 4 gives $(T)=\bigcap_{i=1}^r(t_i)$: parameter primality follows from the factorization lemma, and distinctness from regularity of every permuted parameter sequence. Thus $(T)$ is radical. For $r=0$, $(T)=R$ is radical as well. Moreover $T$ is a nonzero element of the domain $R$, hence a nonzerodivisor, including $T=1$. Every local ring of $H$ is $R/(T)$ by step 1 and is reduced. The stalk definition of reducedness therefore proves that $H$ is reduced.
Cited statements: lem-trf-regular-local-ufd-boundary-factorization, lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence, def-pc-reduced-scheme.

Original parent step 9: Let $J$ be any subset of the finite component index set and $z\in C_J$. Each selected component contains $z$, so step 8 assigns it a distinct parameter at $z$. By the sum-of-ideals calculation of step 1, $\mathcal O_{C_J,z}$ is $\mathcal O_{X,z}$ modulo these $|J|$ parameters. Permute the full parameter system to put them first and apply the parameter-quotient theorem: this local ring is regular of dimension $\dim\mathcal O_{X,z}-|J|$. The intersections are locally Noetherian, since affine quotients of Noetherian rings are Noetherian (lift an ideal to the original ring and project its finite generating list). Consequently the local-ring criterion for a regular scheme proves that every $C_J$ is regular, including each $C_i$. For an empty intersection scheme there is no $z$ to check. For $J=\varnothing$, the intersection is $X$ and its codimension is zero. We now have all clauses of the boundary definition: a reduced effective Cartier ideal, finitely many distinct integral regular components, and regular intersections with the stated dimension equality. This proves the reverse implication and the final assertion.
Cited statements: lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary.

proof.text: For each prime P_i, apply the regular-quotient kernel theorem to obtain a parameter list xs and c ≤ d with P_i generated by xs.take c. The parameter-quotient theorem gives quotient dimension d-c. Comparing with dim(R/P_i)+1=d forces c=1, so choose g_i with P_i=(g_i).

source.place: Tags 00NR and 00NQ; etale.tex Tag 0BIA, converse local-ring argument.

proof.text: Let I be the supremum of the P_i. It is contained in the maximal ideal, including when the family is empty. Apply the regular-quotient kernel theorem to I, obtaining a parameter list xs with I generated by xs.take c. The parameter-quotient dimension formula and the total-dimension hypothesis give d=(d-c)+r. Since c≤d, c=r and r≤d. Replace xs.take r by the list of the g_i. These two lists generate the same ideal I, so appending xs.drop r still generates the maximal ideal. Its length is d. Enumerate this list by Fin d to obtain the simultaneous parameter system with the required first r entries.

source.place: Tags 00NR and 00NQ; etale.tex Tag 0BIA, converse local-ring argument.

proof.text: For an arbitrary subset s of Fin d, list the indices in s first and those in its complement second, and map the resulting list by t. Its length is d and its set of entries equals that of the original parameter list, so it is a regular system of parameters. Its first |s| entries generate span(t(s)). Applying the parameter-quotient theorem proves regularity and dimension d-|s| for this quotient. This includes the empty and full subsets.

source.place: Tag 00NQ; etale.tex Tag 0BIA, forward local-ring argument, intersections.

proof.text: The singleton quotients are regular local and hence domains, so their defining coordinate ideals are prime. A coordinate cannot vanish: otherwise its quotient is R, contradicting the drop from d to d-1. If (t_i)≤(t_j) for distinct indices, the two-coordinate ideal equals (t_j); its quotient would have both dimensions d-2 and d-1. There are at least two coordinates in this case, so these dimensions differ. Thus the coordinate primes are pairwise incomparable. The regular local source is a domain, hence the finite product of the nonzero coordinates is a nonzerodivisor.

source.place: Tags 00NQ and 00NP; dimension-drop version of the parameter argument in etale.tex Tag 0BIA.

proof.text: Induct on a finite set s of selected coordinates to prove that any element in every selected principal ideal is divisible by their product. At an insertion a, write x=t_a b. For each remaining i, primality of (t_i) and incomparability show b lies in (t_i); apply induction. Divisibility by each factor proves the reverse ideal inclusion. Hence the product ideal is the intersection of the coordinate primes, and is radical. Every prime containing the product contains a factor, by primality. Minimality then identifies a minimal prime with that coordinate ideal; conversely incomparability shows that each coordinate ideal is minimal over the product.

source.place: Tag 0BIA, forward local-ring argument; elementary divisibility and minimal-prime calculation.

proof.text: For the selected subset J of Fin r, map it into Fin d by the injective inclusion Fin.castLE. The image has |J| elements, so step 3 proves the stated stratum regularity and dimension. If r=0 the product is 1, its span is the top ideal, and no prime contains it. The ideal-intersection induction and minimal-prime argument already include this empty case.

source.place: Tag 0BIA, forward local-ring argument, intersections; empty-family conventions.

The intersection is proved by an induction using primality, radicality elementwise, and minimal primes from incomparability.
